claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS is an anchor-box-free and proposal-free object detector.
claims.evidence_quote_short: our proposed detector FCOS is anchor box free, as well as proposal free

claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS achieves 44.7% AP using ResNeXt-64x4d-101 with single-model single-scale testing.
claims.evidence_quote_short: FCOS with ResNeXt-64x4d-101 achieves 44.7% in AP with single-model and single-scale testing

claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS surpasses previous one-stage detectors while being much simpler.
claims.evidence_quote_short: surpassing previous one-stage detectors with the advantage of being much simpler

claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS introduces a single-layer center-ness branch to predict a pixel's deviation from its bounding box center.
claims.evidence_quote_short: we introduce a novel “center-ness” branch (only one layer) to predict the deviation of a pixel to the center of its corresponding bounding box

claims.claim_text_normalized: The center-ness branch boosts detection AP from 33.5% to 37.1%.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the center-ness branch can boost AP from 33.5% to 37.1%

claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS outperforms RetinaNet by 2.4% in AP when both use the ResNet-101-FPN backbone.
claims.evidence_quote_short: with ResNet-101-FPN, our FCOS outperforms the RetinaNet with the same backbone ResNet-101-FPN by 2.4% in AP

claims.claim_text_normalized: FCOS eliminates predefined anchor boxes and avoids complicated computations like overlap calculation during training.
claims.evidence_quote_short: By eliminating the pre-defined set of anchor boxes, FCOS completely avoids the complicated computation related to anchor boxes such as calculating overlapping during training

claims.claim_text_normalized: Anchor-based detector performance is sensitive to the sizes, aspect ratios, and number of anchor boxes.
claims.evidence_quote_short: detection performance is sensitive to the sizes, aspect ratios and number of anchor boxes
